chunk_findings.detail: `fail_closed_data` only traverses `Mapping`, `list`, and `tuple`; any other container is returned unchanged. For example, a failed redaction of a value containing a provider secret in a `set`/`frozenset` (`fail_closed_data({"sk-123"})`) returns `{"sk-123"}` with the secret intact. If that set is later rendered into a committed event shard, the raw secret reaches the log, violating the fail-closed requirement. It should traverse sets/frozensets or reject unsupported container types instead of falling through to `return value`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/redact_errors.py:40

chunk_findings.detail: The `openai` pattern `sk-(?:proj-|svcacct-|admin-)?[0-9A-Za-z_-]{20,}` matches any token beginning with `sk-` followed by 20 characters from a permissive alphabet. A legitimate event line containing `[REDACTED]` causes `shape_hit` to return `"openai"`, so `check_event_secrets` will treat a non-secret job/package/file identifier as an OpenAI key and refuse or redact the commit.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py SHAPES openai

chunk_findings.detail: The advertised generic `key = value` shape does not match plain `key` assignments: the prefix alternation is `(?:api[-_]?key|secret|token|passw(?:or)?d)`. Given `key = 1234567890Abcdefghij`, no provider pattern matches and `assigned-secret` misses it, so a long arbitrary secret assigned to the common variable name `key` is not redacted from the committed event log.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py SHAPES assigned-secret

chunk_findings.detail: Provider shape character classes do not allow newlines, so a provider key split across a line wrap bypasses detection. For example `AIzaABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ\n1234567890` is not matched by `shape_hit` on the full text, and a line-by-line check sees two fragments each below the minimum run; the raw pieces still reach the committed event log, violating the fail-closed goal for secrets split across lines.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py shape_hit

chunk_findings.detail: An added shard line whose content begins with `++ ` is misparsed as a `+++` file header. `git diff` emits that file line as `+++ [REDACTED]` (one leading `+` diff marker plus the two leading `+` and space from the content). The branch `raw.startswith("+++ ")` fires, sets `path = raw[4:]`, and never calls `line_hit` on the line. So a staged event shard line `++ [REDACTED]` is completely skipped and the secret is not scanned, allowing the commit to pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce_secrets.py:64

chunk_findings.detail: `git diff --cached` is run without `--no-textconv`. `--no-ext-diff` does not disable textconv; if a `.gitattributes` file gives the event shard path a `diff=<driver>` with a configured `diff.<driver>.textconv`, the diff output `added_hits` sees is the converted output, not the staged raw blob. A textconv command that replaces key-shaped text with `REDACTED` makes `added_hits` see no shape hit while the staged shard retains the raw credential and is committed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce_secrets.py:89

chunk_findings.detail: `--diff-filter=ACMR` excludes the typechange status `T`. A staged change from a symlink `.ddflow/events/1` to a regular file containing `[REDACTED]` is not emitted at all by this command, so `added_hits` is empty and `check_event_secrets` returns `OK`; the secret-containing regular file is committed without being scanned.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce_secrets.py:97

chunk_findings.detail: The new fail-closed branch returns `fail_closed_text()`, while the normal branch returns the two-tuple `red.text, red.total`. A non-`PatternError` exception from `redactor("log", cfg).text(text)`—the exact case this branch is meant to handle—therefore makes `_redact_event_text` return a placeholder string instead of a `(text, total)` tuple. Existing callers that unpack the two-tuple (`redacted_text, redacted_count = _redact_event_text(...)`) will raise `ValueError: too many values to unpack`, so the fail-closed path crashes event logging rather than writing a safe placeholder.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions.py:66

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `S.redact(blob, cfg)[1] == 0` for `blob = "Zm9v" + KEYS["google"] + "bar"`. That string still contains a complete Google API key shape (`AIza` + 35 filler characters) but it is surrounded by adjacent word characters, so the boundary-sensitive shape match is skipped. This is a concrete bypass: an event line such as `{"text":"Zm9vAIzaFAKEFAKEFAKEFAKEFAKEbar"}` will be written unchanged to a shard, and `check_event_secrets`, which uses the same `shape_hit`, will not block it even though the provider key shape is present in the committed log line, violating the intent that provider key shapes never reach the committed event log.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_redact_provider_keys.py:test_a_shape_inside_a_longer_word_is_left_alone

chunk_findings.detail: The `openai` pattern still applies `_L` before `sk-`, so the long, distinctive `sk-proj-`/`sk-svcacct-`/`sk-admin-` prefixes remain left-guarded. The same change removed the guard from `sk-ant-` because a key pasted against other text must still be caught, but an OpenAI project key glued to preceding word text is missed. Given event text `mysk-proj-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz123`, `shape_hit` starts at `sk-proj-...` but the negative lookbehind sees the preceding `y` and rejects the match, so the raw `sk-proj-...` key is neither redacted nor blocked from the committed shard.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py: openai SHAPES entry

chunk_findings.detail: The fail-closed replacement only replaces mapping values; mapping keys are returned unchanged in `return {k: fail_closed_data(v) for k, v in value.items()}`. A provider key appearing as a JSON object key survives, for example `fail_closed_data({"AIza" + "A"*35: "x"})` yields `{"[REDACTED]": "[REDACTED]"}`. When that result is serialized into a committed event shard, the raw `AIza...` key is written to the log, so this fail-closed path still leaks a provider secret despite the “all text” requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/redact_errors.py: fail_closed_data

chunk_findings.detail: The newly added test `test_merging_in_a_line_the_other_parent_already_committed_is_not_refused` encodes a fail-open path. In that scenario a provider key shaped line is committed on branch `other`; the current branch has an unrelated change; `git merge --no-commit other` stages the secret line into the current branch’s event shard. The merge commit therefore adds a provider key line to this branch’s committed event log, but `check_event_secrets` is asserted to return 0. A side branch containing a secret, committed before the guard existed or with hooks bypassed, can be merged into the protected branch without refusal, so the raw secret reaches the committed event log. Filtering against already-committed parents is a commit-check blind spot.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce_secrets.py check_event_secrets

chunk_findings.detail: The revised `openai` pattern still false-positives on harmless `sk-` identifiers that contain a digit. Given a staged event line `{"text": "[REDACTED]"}`, `shape_hit` sees a token starting with `sk-`, at least 20 trailing `[0-9A-Za-z_-]` characters, and the digit `2`, so it returns `"openai"`; `check_event_secrets` will refuse or redact this non-secret identifier. The added test only checks a digitless hyphenated name (`[REDACTED]`), so it does not catch this remaining false positive.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py SHAPES openai

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 3 still holds for the bare key case. `shape_hit("key = 1234567890Abcdefghij")` still produces no `assigned-secret` hit because the alternation omits the plain name `key`. As a result a long secret assigned to the common variable name `key` is neither redacted from event text nor refused in a commit. The round-2 addition of `access/auth/private key` names does not answer that specific probe, and the triage says the omission is deliberate—but that is exactly the remaining defect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py SHAPES assigned-secret
